stem: One source batch is split into two flowering rooms. What should happen to genealogy?
choices: Assign unrelated downstream identities in each room and retain the original batch only as a historical inventory note.
Close the source batch record once the split occurs because downstream lots become the new active traceability units.
Create downstream lot identities that both retain their relationship to the source batch and record the split/movement event linking source to destination.
Keep the source identity only on the larger downstream lot and treat the smaller room as a secondary sublot without genealogy.
rationale: Splitting a source batch creates downstream identities, but genealogy must preserve how each downstream lot originated. The source record should remain linked through the split/movement event so investigators can trace backward and forward. Deleting or selectively retaining the source relationship breaks the chain of identity.
